title: Unchecked uint128() downcasts of bdv*stalkIssuedPerBdv and gauge average ('safeCast unnecessary' comments) verified safe under realistic bounds
description: Two NatSpec 'safeCast not needed / unnecessary' downcasts were re-derived independently rather than trusted: (1) LibConvert._depositTokensForConvert line 540 `uint128(bdv.mul(LibTokenSilo.stalkIssuedPerBdv(token)))` and (2) LibGauge.updateAverageStalkPerBdvPerSeason line 320 `uint128(getAverageGrownStalkPerBdv().mul(BDV_PRECISION).div(targetSeasonsToCatchUp))`. For (1), stalkIssuedPerBdv is on the order of 1e10 (1 stalk = 1e10 micro-units); overflowing uint128 (~3.4e38) would require bdv > ~3.4e28 micro-BDV, i.e. ~3.4e22 Beans of value, which is many orders of magnitude above any plausible Bean supply (~1e13 micro-Beans). For (2), the divided average is similarly bounded. Both casts are therefore safe in practice; flagged only to record that the comments were verified, not accepted, and that the bound is implicit (not enforced) so a future parameter change to stalkIssuedPerBdv could erode the margin.
impact: No issue under current parameters and realistic supply. Truncation would only occur at absurd BDV magnitudes. Documented for completeness and future-parameter caution.

ite.intent: Silently truncate stalk on a uint128 downcast to under-issue or wrap stalk
ite.evasion: Required magnitude is non-physical given Bean supply; not reachable
